sonnet.problem: The opening card says 'Gilead's rulers need somebody to launch the attack'. Card 7 later asks who comes to get Jephthah, and the right answer is 'The elders of Gilead'. The setup already points to the leaders of Gilead and makes the wrong answers (priests of Shiloh, men of Ephraim) easy to rule out.
sonnet.rule: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

sonnet.problem: The right answer 'The LORD delivers Sihon into Israel's hand' is the only one in Bible-style wording, and it is the longest. The wrong answers are plain and modern ('Sihon drives Israel back to Kadesh', 'Moab steps in and stops the fight'), so the right answer stands out.
sonnet.rule: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

sonnet.problem: The card names 'Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab' and then says 'asks if this king thinks he's so much better than Balak'. 'This king' reads as Balak, so the sentence says Balak is asking whether Balak is better than Balak. The baker can't tell that it means the king of the Ammonites.
sonnet.rule: Clear English. Every card reads correctly. ... "He," "she" and "they" always point to someone the baker can tell.
